To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed two novel sensors for the detection of Ni2+, Cr3+ and CN− in organic media.
two novel rhodamine based probes have been developed for the detection of Ni2+, Cr3+ and CN− in organic media.
two new rhodamine-based sensors have been designed for Ni2+ or Cr3+ detection, and the latter can be used to detect CN− by the metal displacement approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new rhodamine based turn-on sensors for the detection of metal ions.
the synthesis of novel fluorescent probes for metal ions.
the synthesis and characterization of new rhodamine derivatives, which have been used as sensors for metal ions and anions.

these sensors are useful for the detection of Ni2+, Cr3+, CN− and Hg2+ ions, in organic media, and that the detection of these ions is achieved through the metal displacement and the fluorescence quenching approach.
the rhodamine based probes described in this work can be used for the detection of Ni2+, Cr3+ and CN− in organic media, while 1 can be used for Cu2+ detection as well.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel class of rhodamine based fluorescent sensors for Ni2+ in organic medium.
the rhodamine B based sensors 1 and 2 have been designed to selectively and sensitively detect Ni2+ and/or Cr3+, and the latter is further used for detecting CN−.

the rhodamine-based sensor 1 can detect CN− in the presence of Ni2+ by the metal-displacement approach, and the rhodamine-quinoline based sensor 2 can detect CN− by the metal-displacing approach in the presence of Cr3+.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metal displacement strategy can be used to design turn-on probes for anions in organic media, provided that the metal complex formed is non-fluorescence and the resulting complex is fluorescent.
we have developed two novel rhodamine-based probes which can be used for the detection of Ni2+, Cr3+ and CN−.
the combination of the rhodamine and quinoline moieties in the same molecule allows for the detection of two different metals and CN−.
